it_bit_mask — 2D gray op

• Data kinds: image → image

• Call: fullseye.apply(img, "it_bit_mask", a=0.5, b=0.5) (the 2-D model is one image plus two scalar knobs a,b∈[0,1])

• HALCON equivalent: bit_mask (the HALCON reference is a useful guide to its meaning and parameters)

Usage

bit_mask: logical AND of the 8-bit image with the constant bit mask round(a*255). b is ignored.

After bringing the input to 2-D float64 in [0,1], quantizes it with round(x*255) to 8-bit integers in 0 to 255, takes a per-pixel bitwise AND with the constant mask m = round(a*255) & 0xFF (a is clipped to [0,1]), and returns to [0,1] with /255. a=1 gives mask 255 (identity except for quantization), a=0 mask 0 (all zero), a=0.5 gives 128 (keeps only the most significant bit = same as 2-level binarization by whether >= 0.5 or not). b is unused.

Returns float64 of the same shape as the input, with discrete values k/255. a acts as a bit pattern, so it is not monotonic: 0.5 (=128) keeps the most significant bit, around 0.25 (=64) only the 2nd bit from the top, and each yields an independent striped grey-level plane (bit plane). To "keep the upper n bits", choose a = (256 - 2**(8-n))/255 (192/255 ≈ 0.753 for n=2). Colour (3-D) input is reduced to 2-D by channel averaging. On exception it is fail-soft: a clipped version of the input is returned and recorded in the ledger. Bit shifts are it_bit_lshift / it_bit_rshift; reducing the number of grey levels is it_convert_image_type. For analysing watermarks and steganography, or for visualising quantization noise (extracting lower bit planes).
